subject: Urgent: Sentinel burst contention — request for priority lane and sizing confirmation
messages:
From: Kate Reynolds <kate@sentinel.ai>
To: sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai
Cc: cloud-ops@sentinel.ai
Date: Wed, 12 Aug 2026 09:13:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Capacity plan for Q4 — urgent follow-up

Sergio — thanks again for the call this morning. We're into PoC week and are seeing sustained token throughput that's above our expected envelope. Two asks from my side: 

1) Can Redwood confirm whether our Dedicated tranche can be bumped to a higher priority lane this month? We are seeing sub-2s p99 latency slips when our training bursts overlap with other tenants.
2) We need a formal sizing note and confirmation of preempt behavior for dedicated GPUs tied to SENT-4372 so we can clear procurement and keep the pilot schedule.

Attaching a short snapshot of our observed traffic (capacity_snapshot_20260812.csv). Happy to hop on a quick sync — Kate

-- 
Kate Reynolds
Head of Cloud Ops, Sentinel AI
kate@sentinel.ai | +1 (415) 555-0191

From: sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai
To: Kate Reynolds <kate@sentinel.ai>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 12 Aug 2026 10:07:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Capacity plan for Q4 — urgent follow-up

Kate — appreciate the data and flag. TL;DR: we can offer a temporary priority lane for the pilot window but need to confirm exact GPU counts and make a small change to your rollout schedule to avoid preemption windows. Proposed next steps below.

Summary of actions we can take now:
- Short-term (this week): provision a priority lane on Dedicated pool B (US-west) for 08/14–08/28 with non-preemptible mode during 06:00–18:00 PT for live traffic.
- Sizing ask: we need the average sustained concurrent model tokens/sec and peak burst duration (CSV helps). From a back-of-envelope: the numbers in your CSV map to ~6 A100-equivalent GPUs to hit your p99 target during bursts; allow +1 GPU for safety.
- Procurement note: we'll issue a formal sizing & preempt behavior doc for legal/finance (sentinel_sla_request_v2.pdf).

Open question for Karthik + Laura: can we commit the priority lane without breaking current tranche SLAs for other reserved customers? If not, what's the minimal compensating action (e.g., transient burst throttles or scheduled ramp windows)?

I'll schedule a 30m call if helpful. Sergio

--
Sergio Alvarez
Account Executive, Dedicated & Enterprise
Redwood Inference
sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai | +1 (650) 555-0112

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
To: sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 12 Aug 2026 11:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Capacity plan for Q4 — urgent follow-up

Sergio/Laura — quick internal note before we commit externally. Current Dedicated pool B commitments:
- Reserved: 48 A100-eq GPUs across three enterprise deals (Aurora, Helix, Sentinel tranche).
- Headroom: ~6 GPUs available for short-term bursts; another 4 are tagged as "soft-reserve" for enterprise burst contracts.

Options and risks: 
1) Provide Sentinel the 6 GPUs as a priority lane for 2 weeks. Risk: Helix (deal HXL-198) may trigger a scheduled training job on 08/20 that requires 4 GPUs; if both overlap we either preempt the priority lane or throttle Helix.
2) Offer 4 guaranteed GPUs + 2 on best-effort. This reduces p99 risk for Sentinel but leaves some residual latency exposure.
3) Timebox the non-preemptible window to business hours only (as Sergio suggested) and require Sentinel to shift bulk training to off-hours. This is the safest for fairness but requires customer operational changes.

Recommendation: go with option 2 + require Sentinel to accept a fallback plan (auto-fail to a slightly lower quantized model variant) and a 10% credit if p99 exceeds target. That minimizes cross-customer disruption. Laura — can you confirm whether credits fall under our allowable commercial exceptions?

Karthik

--
Karthik Iyer
Director, Capacity Planning
Redwood Inference

From: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
To: Kate Reynolds <kate@sentinel.ai>, sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 13 Aug 2026 16:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Capacity plan for Q4 — urgent follow-up

Kate / team — following internal review we've agreed the pragmatic path below. We're locking it in now so procurement/legal have the facts for SENT-4372. Please treat this as our official confirmatory note: 

Final decision (effective 08/14–08/28):
- Allocation: 4 guaranteed A100-equivalent GPUs in Dedicated pool B + 2 best-effort GPUs during peak windows.
- Non-preemptible window: 06:00–18:00 PT for live inference traffic (these 4 guaranteed GPUs will not be preempted in that window). Outside the window we may reallocate the best-effort GPUs.
- Fallback policy: during an overlap that exceeds available capacity we will route to a quantized variant (q4_16) automatically; we will only preempt best-effort GPUs.
- Credits: if p99 latency exceeds agreed threshold for more than 3 business hours in a 7-day rolling window, Redwood will issue a service credit equal to 10% of that week's dedicated usage fees.

Action items: 
- Sentinel to confirm acceptance and whether you can shift any heavy training to off-peak windows (08/18–08/22 suggested).
- Sergio to attach the formal sizing & preempt doc (we'll put the signed SLA into the HubSpot deal record).

Kate — once you confirm, Ben will open the capacity change ticket and Karthik will schedule the provisioning.

Thanks — Laura

--
Laura Bennett
Head of Customer Success, Enterprise
Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0133
